title: Ferrofluid Speaker
description: The desktop ferrofluid-speaker gadget: a grey enclosure with a bright, backlit circular window, black ferrofluid sitting on the lit glass while an electromagnet behind the centre pulls it into a clustered, glossy central mass ringed by satellite droplets. The music drives the field — on the bass the drops rush inward and the mass throws out reaching arms and spikes, then relaxes and scatters into beads between hits. The fluid is a metaball field so nearby drops merge with smooth necks, shaded like oily black chrome with a wet white specular, a cool rim where the lumps catch the lit window, and a soft contact shadow seating it on the glass. Turn on the mic to drive it live; with no mic it runs on a synthetic kick so it always dances. Audio drive, magnet pull, droplet count, fluid amount, spread, reach/spikes, viscosity and sheen hue are live.
